story: In the 1980s, NASA's Pioneer 10 and 11 probes began slowing down mysteriously as they left the solar system. This "Pioneer Anomaly" baffled scientists for decades, suggesting our fundamental understanding of gravity might be wrong. The spacecraft were drifting sunward by thousands of kilometers every year, defying predictions. Was it dark matter? New physics? A breakdown of Einstein's relativity? Finally, in 2012, the mystery was solved. It wasn't exotic gravity, but mundane heat. The probes' nuclear power generators radiated warmth unevenly, creating a tiny photon pressure pushing them back toward the Sun. Recovering old magnetic tapes found under staircases and funding from The Planetary Society helped prove standard physics still held true. The universe wasn't broken; the spacecraft were simply radiating heat asymmetrically.
